notes: Granularity: unit/section names plus the named sub-headings of broad units (e.g. JEE's 'Organic Compounds Containing Oxygen' -> Alcohols/Phenols/Ethers, Aldehydes and Ketones, Carboxylic Acids); illustrative sub-bullets are not recorded. Bare discipline banners (Physical/Inorganic/Organic Chemistry) are not recorded as topic lines for JEE Main / NEET / JEE Advanced; GATE and CSIR numbered section units ARE recorded as lines.
GA exclusions: GATE General Aptitude (Section GA) and CSIR NET Part A general-aptitude lines are excluded per the register's rules; only chemistry subject topics are recorded.

JEE Advanced: jeeadv.ac.in was visited but is currently in its 2027 pre-announcement state (the syllabus.html URL serves scribe-services boilerplate; no syllabus page published, /archive.html only lists past papers); the syllabus has been unchanged since the 2023 revision, so two reputable mirrors were used — Vedantu (carries the syllabus verbatim) and Physics Wallah (corroborates the topic index). Both marked 'mirror'.

IB: ibo.org is Cloudflare-gated and unreachable from this environment (checked via HTTP and a headless browser); the official 2023 DP Chemistry structure (Structure 1-3 / Reactivity 1-3, first assessment 2025) was taken from the SaveMyExams mirror of the syllabus (marked 'mirror'). The Tools and Inquiry-process skills sections are consolidated into two summary lines rather than exploded.
NEET UG 2026 chemistry syllabus is unit-for-unit identical to the JEE Main chemistry syllabus (the same 20 NTA units); each is recorded under its own exam as the ledger requires.
CUET UG 2026 official PDF heads the domain as 'Chemistry - 306' (the domain code was 304 in earlier cycles).

IChO: Appendix C of the IChO Regulations (valid from 1 August 2023) exported from the official Google Doc linked at ichosc.org/regulations; the general-skilled lines (awareness of experimental errors/significant figures, secondary-school mathematics skills) are skipped as general aptitude, and the laboratory-skills register and the fields-of-advanced-difficulty example lists are consolidated into single summary lines.
AP Chemistry uses the College Board Course and Exam Description effective Fall 2024 (unit names differ from the pre-2024 CED); the science practices are skills, not topic lines.
A-levels: Cambridge 9701 syllabus for 2025-2027 (official PDF from cambridgeinternational.org); A Level-only repeats of AS topic names are suffixed '(A Level)'.

Re-derivation records 310 topic lines vs the original pass's 246 — the overshoot comes from the verbatim breadth of the JEE Advanced section list (37 lines), the Cambridge 9701 numbered topic list (37) and the IChO Appendix C knowledge list (55).

Nucleons, isotopes, radioactive decay and nuclear reactions (alpha, beta, gamma)
Quantum numbers (n, l, m) and orbitals (s, p, d) in hydrogen-like atoms; Hund's rule, Pauli exclusion principle
Electronic configuration of main group and the first-row transition metal atoms and their ions
Periodic table and trends (electronegativity, electron affinity, ionization energy, atomic and ionic size, melting points, metallic character, reactivity)
Bond types (covalent, ionic, metallic, coordination), intermolecular forces and relation to properties
Lewis theory; molecular structures and VSEPR theory
Balancing equations, empirical formulae, mole concept and Avogadro constant, stoichiometric calculations, density, calculations with different concentration units
Chemical equilibrium, Le Chatelier's principle, equilibrium constants in terms of concentrations, pressures and mole fractions

Arrhenius and Bronsted acid-base theory, pH, self-ionization of water, equilibrium constants of acid-base reactions, pH of weak acid solutions, pH of very dilute solutions and simple buffer solutions, hydrolysis of salts
Complexation reactions, definition of coordination number, complex formation constants
Partition coefficients: definition and simple calculations
Basics of electrochemistry: electromotive force, Nernst equation, electrolysis, Faraday's laws
Rate of chemical reactions, elementary reactions, factors affecting the reaction rate, rate law for homogeneous and heterogeneous reactions, rate constant, reaction order
Reaction energy profile, activation energy, Arrhenius equation, catalysis, influence of a catalyst on thermodynamic and kinetic characteristics of a reaction
Use of simple first-order and zeroth-order kinetic rate laws, exponential decay, half-lives
Energy, heat and work, enthalpy and energy, heat capacity, Hess's law, Born-Haber cycle, standard formation enthalpies, solution, solvation and bond enthalpies
Definition and concept of entropy and Gibbs' energy, second law of thermodynamics, direction of spontaneous change; calculation of equilibrium constants from standard enthalpy and entropy data
Principles of direct and indirect titration (back titration)
Acidimetry and alkalimetry, acidimetric titration curves, choice and color of indicators for acidimetry
Redox titrations (permanganometric and iodometric); iodometry (reaction of thiosulfate and iodine)
Basic principles of inorganic qualitative analysis for ions specified in factual knowledge, flame tests; identification of Ag+, Ba2+, Fe3+, Cu2+, Cl-, CO32-, SO42-
Basic concepts of light and color, wavelength, frequency, wave numbers, photon energies, Lambert-Beer law
Reactions of s-block elements with water, oxygen and halogens, their color in flame tests
Stoichiometry, reactions and properties of binary non-metal hydrides
Common reactions of carbon, nitrogen and sulfur oxides (CO, CO2, NO, NO2, N2O4, SO2, SO3)
Common oxidation states of p-block elements, stoichiometry of common halides and oxoacids; reaction of halogens with water
Common oxidation states of first row transition metals and the color of these ions; dissolution of these metals and Al, amphoteric hydroxides (Al(OH)3, Cr(OH)3, Zn(OH)2)
Permanganate, chromate, dichromate ions and their redox reactions

Organic structure-reactivity relations (polarity, electrophilicity, nucleophilicity, inductive effects, relative stability), structure-property relations (boiling point, acidity, basicity); common electrophiles and nucleophiles
Hybridization and geometry at carbon and other centers
Sigma and pi bonds, delocalization, aromaticity, resonance structures
Stereochemistry (E/Z, cis/trans isomers, chirality, optical activity, Cahn-Ingold-Prelog system, Fischer projections, D/L); cyclohexane conformations
Electrophilic addition: addition to double and triple bonds, regioselectivity (Markovnikoff/Kharasch rule), stereochemistry
Electrophilic substitution: substitution on aromatic rings, influence of substituents on the reactivity and regioselectivity, electrophilic species
Elimination: E1 and E2 reactions at sp3 carbon centers, stereochemistry, acid-base catalysis, common leaving groups
Nucleophilic substitution: SN1 and SN2 reactions at sp3 carbon centers, stereochemistry
Nucleophilic addition: addition to carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom double and triple bonds, addition-elimination reactions, acid-base catalysis
Radical substitution: reaction of halogens with alkanes
Oxidations and reductions: switching between the different oxidation levels of common functional groups
Grignard reaction, Fehling and Tollens reaction
Simple polymers and their preparation (polystyrene, polyethylene, polyamides, polyesters); polymers and monomers, chain polymerizations, polyaddition and polycondensation
Amino acids and their classification in groups, isoelectric point, peptide bond, peptides and proteins
Carbohydrates: open chain and cyclic forms; structures of glucose and fructose
Lipids: general formulae of di- and triacyl glycerides, saturated and unsaturated fatty acids
General structure of DNA and RNA, hydrogen bonding between bases, the concept of replication and transcription
Use of common protecting groups in organic synthesis
Hydrophilic and hydrophobic groups, micelle and bilayer formation

Laboratory skills expected to be known by all participants (heating and reflux, mass and volume measurement, preparation and dilution of solutions, titrations, pH measurement, filtration, drying of precipitates, instrument operation, graphing and analysis of experimental data)

Fields of advanced difficulty releasable only via the annual preparatory problems (inorganic stereochemistry, solid state structures and Bragg's law, crystal field theory, thermodynamic cycles, Latimer/Frost/Pourbaix diagrams, advanced kinetics and kinetic theory, phase diagrams, advanced stereochemistry and stereoselective synthesis, pericyclic reactions, advanced polymers, saccharides, protein structure and enzymes, complex solubility, quantum mechanics, spectroscopy MS/IR/NMR; practical: TLC, column chromatography, extraction, recrystallization, distillation, viscometry)
